overall: The AG found the commission chair violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating via emails sent to a quorum on October 7 and 27, and ordered compliance and public release of the emails.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the commission chair deliberated by email with a quorum on October 7 by sending procedures for handling member conflicts of interest.
allegations.key_passage: Here, we find that Mr. Batchelor’s emails sent on October 7 and 27 to a quorum of the Commission concerned the Commission’s operation including how it would handle conflicts of interest and Mr. Batchelor’s plan to request dismissal of Mr. Harrington if he did not follow the proposed procedures.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the commission chair deliberated by email with a quorum on October 27 by responding to a member's recusal statement with conflict-of-interest instructions.
allegations.key_passage: This was public business within the Commission’s jurisdiction and therefore the October 7 and 27 emails discussing such business violated the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law ordered for the Commission
Caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law
Release to the public of the October 7 and 27 emails, by reading them aloud at an open meeting or attaching them to the minutes of an open meeting
remedy_passage: Additionally, we order the Commission to release to the public the October 7 and 27 emails, either by reading them aloud at an open meeting, or by attaching the emails to the minutes of an open meeting.
